title: LivaNova S5 Heart-Lung Machine - Console Will Not Power On or a Module Does Not Start
description: Troubleshoots loss of console power or a module that fails to initialize, focusing on external power, connections, configuration, and safe substitution.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Perfusion Capability
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot an S5 console or module while a patient depends on the affected function. If the problem occurs during a case, immediately follow the facility perfusion contingency plan and transfer the affected function to verified backup equipment. If there is smoke, unusual odor, excessive heat, liquid intrusion, arcing, or visible electrical damage, disconnect the equipment from power when clinically safe and remove it from service. Expected outcome: Patient support is maintained independently of the malfunctioning console or module. If clinical support has been safely transferred and the affected equipment is no longer required for patient care, troubleshooting may continue.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Power or Startup Failure
steps.instructions: Identify whether: The entire console is unpowered. Some modules start while one module remains inactive. The system begins startup but stops before normal operation. Indicators illuminate briefly and then extinguish. The failure follows movement, cleaning, reconfiguration, or connection of another component. Record any displayed message or abnormal indicator exactly as shown. Expected outcome: The failure is isolated to the complete console, a specific module, or the startup sequence. If the system starts normally after confirming the reported condition and remains stable through functional verification, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 3. Verify Facility AC Power
steps.instructions: Inspect the power cord, plug, strain relief, and accessible power connections for damage or looseness. Confirm the device is connected to an appropriate powered receptacle and verify the receptacle using approved test equipment or a known-good facility power source. Avoid using unapproved extension cords or adapters. Expected outcome: Stable facility power is available and the external power path is intact. If restoring a loose or unavailable AC source returns the system to normal operation and verification passes, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 4. Inspect External Power and Module Connections
steps.instructions: With the system safely removed from clinical use, inspect accessible console and module connections. Look for: Partially seated connectors Bent or damaged connector shells Contamination Pin damage visible without disassembly Loose retaining hardware Cable strain or crushing Reseat only user-accessible or service-approved external connections. Expected outcome: All required external connections are secure, clean, and undamaged. If reseating an external connection restores normal startup and repeated power cycles are successful, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 5. Isolate the Affected Module
steps.instructions: Determine whether the startup problem remains associated with one module, cable, or console position. When permitted by approved procedures, compare operation using a known-good compatible module, cable, or connection point. Do not interchange components unless compatibility is established. Expected outcome: The problem either follows the suspect external component or remains with the console/module position. If a known-good substitution identifies a defective external component and the system operates normally after replacement, troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 6. Check Controls and System Configuration
steps.instructions: Verify that externally accessible power controls, module enable states, and normal clinical configuration are appropriate. Confirm no component has been intentionally disabled, disconnected, or removed from the configured system. Do not enter restricted service menus or alter protected configuration parameters without authorization. Expected outcome: The system is configured for the installed modules and no obvious control or configuration condition prevents startup. If correcting an authorized configuration issue restores normal startup, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 7. Evaluate Battery-Supported Startup Behavior
steps.instructions: If the system incorporates battery-backed operation, compare behavior on verified AC power and battery-supported operation as permitted by approved procedures. Note whether the problem occurs only during one power source condition. Do not intentionally deplete backup power needed for clinical readiness. Expected outcome: The console and installed modules behave consistently on the available approved power sources. If the failure is isolated to an external power source or replaceable approved battery component and correction restores normal operation, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After correction, power-cycle the system according to normal operating procedures and verify: Console startup completes. Required modules initialize. Displays and indicators operate. No unexpected alarms or communication failures remain. Pumps and monitoring modules required for clinical use respond appropriately during a controlled test. Complete applicable return-to-service testing before releasing the system. Expected outcome: The S5 completes startup reliably and all required modules are available and stable. If all checks pass, troubleshooting is complete.

steps.title: 9. Escalate an Unresolved Startup Failure
steps.instructions: If the console remains unpowered, startup repeatedly fails, or a module remains unavailable after external causes are ruled out, stop troubleshooting. Do not proceed into internal power supplies, backplanes, circuit boards, or internal communication hardware unless specifically authorized and trained for manufacturer-level service. Expected outcome: The device remains controlled and unavailable for clinical use until qualified service evaluation is completed.

CCR.Complaint: Perfusion reported that the LivaNova S5 console powered on but one installed module did not start.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the affected module's external connection partially seated after the console had been moved.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering reseated and secured the connection, completed repeated startup and functional checks, and verified the module initialized normally.

helpfulDetails: Entire console or specific module affected
Whether the system had recently been moved or reconfigured

title: LivaNova S5 Heart-Lung Machine - Roller Pump Will Not Run or Speed Is Unstable
description: Troubleshoots a roller pump that will not start or maintain stable speed, emphasizing controls, tubing setup, connections, and safe external checks.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Perfusion
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot an unreliable roller pump while it is supporting a patient. If the condition develops during bypass, immediately follow the perfusion contingency plan and transition flow to a verified alternate pumping method or backup system. Stop using any pump exhibiting uncontrolled speed, unexpected starts or stops, severe mechanical noise, smoke, odor, or visible damage. Expected outcome: Patient circulation is supported by reliable equipment before technical troubleshooting begins. Once the affected pump is isolated from patient support, troubleshooting may continue.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Pump Behavior
steps.instructions: Determine whether the pump: Does not start. Starts but immediately stops. Runs intermittently. Displays changing speed while mechanically stable. Physically surges or varies speed. Responds inconsistently to its control. Fails only under tubing load. Record any system message or alarm exactly. Expected outcome: The failure is clearly characterized as command, display, load-related, or actual mechanical speed instability. If the pump operates normally during controlled reproduction and remains stable through verification, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Pump Head and Tubing Setup
steps.instructions: With the pump stopped and removed from clinical use, inspect the accessible pump head and tubing path. Verify: Correct compatible tubing is being used. Tubing is seated correctly. Tubing is not twisted, kinked, flattened, or excessively stretched. No foreign material is interfering with roller movement. The pump head area is clean and unobstructed. Do not adjust occlusion beyond authorized procedures. Expected outcome: The pump head rotates freely through its normal accessible range and the tubing is properly positioned. If correcting tubing placement restores smooth, stable operation, troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 4. Verify Pump Controls
steps.instructions: Confirm the pump's normal operating controls are enabled and positioned correctly. Check for: Stop or standby state Speed control position Direction selection when applicable Any externally accessible emergency or safety control that may inhibit operation Do not bypass safety interlocks. Expected outcome: The pump is commanded to run using normal controls and no external control state is preventing operation. If correcting a control setting restores normal speed control, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 5. Inspect External Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible cables and connectors associated with the pump module for looseness, damage, contamination, or strain. Reseat approved external connectors with the system safely out of clinical use. Expected outcome: Pump power and communication connections are secure and undamaged. If reseating an external connection restores reliable operation, troubleshooting can stop after repeated functional testing.

steps.title: 6. Compare With a Known-Good Setup
steps.instructions: When permitted, test the pump using a known-good compatible tubing setup or compare the suspect pump channel with another functioning S5 roller pump under controlled bench conditions. Do not use patient circuits for troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The problem is shown to follow the tubing/accessory setup or remain with the pump assembly. If an external setup issue is identified and corrected, troubleshooting can stop once performance is verified.

steps.title: 7. Observe Operation Without Excessive Load
steps.instructions: Using approved test conditions, command the pump through a reasonable operating range and observe whether rotation is smooth and responsive. Stop testing immediately if there is: Grinding Binding Irregular rotation Sudden speed change Excessive vibration Burning odor Unexpected shutdown Expected outcome: The pump responds smoothly and consistently to speed commands without abnormal sound or vibration. If operation remains stable through the controlled test, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Verify: Pump starts and stops correctly. Speed control changes are predictable. Displayed speed is stable. Mechanical rotation appears consistent. Tubing remains properly retained. Relevant alarms or safety functions are available. Complete required return-to-service testing before clinical use. Expected outcome: Roller pump operation is stable, controllable, and repeatable. If all checks pass, troubleshooting is complete.

steps.title: 9. Escalate Persistent Pump Instability
steps.instructions: If the pump will not run, speed remains unstable, or abnormal mechanical behavior persists after external setup, controls, and connections are ruled out, remove it from service. Do not disassemble the drive mechanism, motor, encoder, control electronics, or internal pump assembly without authorized service procedures. Expected outcome: An unreliable pump is prevented from returning to patient use.

CCR.Complaint: Perfusion reported that an S5 roller pump speed fluctuated during pre-case setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the pump tubing twisted where it entered the roller head, creating uneven mechanical loading.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering corrected the tubing routing and verified smooth, stable pump operation through repeated speed changes during bench testing.

helpfulDetails: Tubing position in the pump head
Whether instability occurred only under load

title: LivaNova S5 Heart-Lung Machine - Centrifugal Pump Drive Not Recognized or Stops Unexpectedly
description: Troubleshoots centrifugal pump drive recognition or unexpected stopping by checking power, connections, compatible accessories, controls, and communication before escalation.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Circulatory Support
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot an unreliable centrifugal pump drive while it is providing patient flow. If the drive stops or becomes unrecognized during clinical use, immediately execute the facility perfusion backup plan and establish flow using verified alternate equipment. Do not repeatedly restart a drive that stops unexpectedly during patient support. Expected outcome: Patient circulation is maintained independently of the suspect centrifugal pump drive. Once the affected drive is no longer supporting the patient, troubleshooting may continue.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether: The drive is absent from the system at startup. It is initially recognized but later disappears. The pump starts and then stops. A display or module indicates loss of communication. Recognition changes when the cable is moved. The problem began after equipment relocation or accessory replacement. Record any displayed message exactly. Expected outcome: The problem is categorized as startup recognition, intermittent connection, or unexpected stopping. If recognition returns and remains stable through repeated controlled testing, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 3. Verify Power and Module Readiness
steps.instructions: Confirm the S5 console and associated pump-control hardware are fully powered and have completed normal startup. Check that the affected drive is connected to the expected powered system configuration. Expected outcome: The supporting console and control module are operational and ready to communicate with the centrifugal drive. If restoring normal system power resolves the issue, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Drive Cable and Connectors
steps.instructions: With the equipment safely out of clinical use, inspect accessible drive and system cables for: Loose connectors Damaged connector shells Bent or contaminated contacts visible externally Cable cuts or crushing Strain near connector ends Evidence of fluid intrusion Reseat only approved external connections. Expected outcome: The drive connections are secure and free of visible damage. If reseating a connection restores reliable recognition and controlled operation, troubleshooting can stop after repeated verification.

steps.title: 5. Verify the Pump Head and Disposable Interface
steps.instructions: Inspect the compatible centrifugal pump head and its seating in the drive. Confirm it is correctly positioned, fully engaged, undamaged, and free of foreign material at the interface. Do not troubleshoot using a patient-connected disposable circuit. Expected outcome: The disposable pump head interfaces correctly with the drive and does not create an obvious mechanical or recognition problem. If correcting seating or replacing a defective disposable with a known-good compatible item restores operation, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 6. Compare With Known-Good Compatible Components
steps.instructions: When permitted by approved procedures, substitute a known-good compatible drive cable, pump head, or drive assembly one component at a time. Maintain clear control of which component is being tested. Expected outcome: The problem follows one replaceable external component or remains with the original drive/system connection. If a defective external component is identified and replaced successfully, troubleshooting can stop after final functional testing.

steps.title: 7. Check Normal Controls and Configuration
steps.instructions: Verify that the centrifugal pump function is enabled and configured as expected for the installed system. Confirm no externally accessible stop condition or control selection is preventing operation. Do not alter restricted configuration or bypass safety functions. Expected outcome: The drive is correctly enabled within the normal operating configuration. If an authorized control or configuration correction restores stable function, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 8. Perform Controlled Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Under approved bench conditions, verify: Drive recognition remains stable. The pump starts and stops normally. Speed commands produce predictable response. No unexpected interruptions occur. Cables remain stationary and secure. Relevant alarms or status indications function. Expected outcome: The centrifugal pump drive remains recognized and operates reliably during repeated testing. If all checks pass, troubleshooting is complete.

steps.title: 9. Escalate Persistent Recognition or Shutdown Problems
steps.instructions: If recognition remains intermittent or the drive stops unexpectedly after external components and connections are ruled out, remove the system from service. Do not disassemble the drive motor, internal sensors, communication circuitry, or module electronics without authorized service procedures. Expected outcome: Unreliable centrifugal pump equipment is prevented from returning to patient care.

CCR.Complaint: Perfusion reported that the S5 centrifugal pump drive was intermittently not recognized during setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external drive cable connector was not fully seated at the system connection.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering reseated and secured the connection and verified consistent drive recognition and normal operation through repeated bench testing.

helpfulDetails: Whether the drive stopped while running

title: LivaNova S5 Heart-Lung Machine - Pump Occlusion, Tubing Wear, or Excessive Pump Noise
description: Addresses abnormal pump noise, visible tubing wear, and suspected occlusion by checking circuit setup, pump-head condition, tubing path, and mechanical loading.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Circuit
steps.instructions: Do not investigate pump occlusion, tubing damage, or abnormal pump noise while a patient depends on the affected pumping circuit. Follow the perfusion contingency plan and establish reliable alternate support before removing or manipulating tubing. If tubing shows visible damage, excessive wear, cracking, flattening, or compromise, treat the circuit as unsafe according to clinical protocol. Expected outcome: Patient flow is maintained and the suspect pump/tubing interface is isolated from clinical use. Once the system is safe, troubleshooting may continue.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Condition
steps.instructions: Determine whether the primary problem is: Excessive pump noise Tubing wear Flattening or deformation Apparent over-occlusion Slippage Vibration Pump-head binding Noise only at specific speeds Record when the issue occurs and whether it is reproducible. Expected outcome: The condition is clearly characterized before adjustments are considered. If the issue cannot be reproduced and the complete setup passes controlled verification, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Tubing
steps.instructions: With the pump stopped, inspect the tubing through the roller-pump path for: Twisting Kinks Flattened areas Abrasion Surface wear Incorrect routing Foreign material Improper size or compatibility Do not reuse compromised tubing. Expected outcome: Tubing is appropriate, correctly routed, and free of visible damage. If replacing or correctly routing the tubing eliminates the abnormal condition, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Verify Tubing Placement in the Pump Head
steps.instructions: Check that tubing is seated consistently in the roller path and is not trapped against guards or adjacent hardware. Do not make unauthorized occlusion adjustments. Expected outcome: Tubing is centered and properly retained through the pump-head path. If proper seating eliminates noise or uneven tubing loading, troubleshooting can stop after controlled testing.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Accessible Pump Head
steps.instructions: Examine the external pump-head surfaces, rollers, guards, and accessible moving areas for: Contamination Foreign material Visible wear Cracks Loose external hardware Misalignment visible without disassembly Rotate or operate the pump only under approved safe conditions. Expected outcome: The pump head is clean, unobstructed, and has no obvious external mechanical damage. If cleaning or removing an external obstruction restores quiet, smooth operation, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 6. Compare With Known-Good Tubing
steps.instructions: Use a known-good compatible tubing segment or approved test circuit to determine whether the condition follows the tubing or remains with the pump. Do not use a patient circuit for this comparison. Expected outcome: The cause is isolated to the disposable tubing/setup or to the pump assembly. If known-good tubing eliminates the condition, replace the defective or inappropriate tubing and complete verification.

steps.title: 7. Evaluate Pump Operation Under Controlled Conditions
steps.instructions: Run the pump using an approved bench setup and observe for: Grinding Rhythmic knocking Squealing Vibration Uneven roller movement Tubing migration Visible recurring deformation Stop testing if mechanical binding or significant abnormal noise persists. Expected outcome: Pump operation is smooth and tubing remains properly positioned without abnormal wear. If operation is normal and repeatable, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Verify that the pump: Starts and stops correctly. Runs smoothly across a controlled operating range. Does not produce excessive noise. Does not cause abnormal tubing movement or visible wear. Maintains proper tubing retention. Complete any applicable return-to-service checks. Expected outcome: Pump mechanics and tubing interaction are stable and appropriate for clinical use. If all checks pass, troubleshooting is complete.

steps.title: 9. Escalate Mechanical Abnormalities
steps.instructions: If excessive noise, binding, roller irregularity, or recurring tubing damage persists with known-good compatible tubing, remove the affected pump from service. Do not disassemble bearings, drive components, roller assemblies, or internal mechanisms without authorized manufacturer procedures. Expected outcome: Equipment with unresolved mechanical behavior remains unavailable for patient use.

CCR.Complaint: Perfusion reported excessive noise from an S5 roller pump and visible tubing movement during setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the tubing twisted and riding against the edge of the pump-head path.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering replaced and correctly routed the test tubing, then verified smooth, quiet pump operation without tubing migration.

title: LivaNova S5 Heart-Lung Machine - Bubble Detector Alarm or Detector Test Failure
description: Troubleshoots bubble detector alarms and failed detector checks by examining sensor placement, tubing compatibility, contamination, connections, and configuration.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Treat the Alarm as Valid
steps.instructions: Do not assume a bubble detector alarm is false during patient support. Follow the perfusion protocol immediately and ensure the circuit is safe before investigating the equipment. Do not bypass or disable a bubble detector to continue clinical use. Expected outcome: Patient protection is maintained and the alarm is managed clinically before technical troubleshooting begins. Once the affected detector is no longer required for active patient support, troubleshooting may continue.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Detector Problem
steps.instructions: Determine whether the issue is: A bubble alarm with no visible bubble Failure of a detector self-test or functional test Detector not recognized Intermittent alarm Alarm only when tubing is moved Alarm after changing tubing or circuit setup Record any message exactly as displayed. Expected outcome: The detector problem is clearly characterized and reproducible. If the detector subsequently passes repeated approved testing with the correct setup, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 3. Inspect Tubing Position in the Detector
steps.instructions: Verify that the intended compatible tubing is fully and correctly seated in the detector. Check for: Partial insertion Tubing off-center Kinks Tubing deformation Unexpected gaps Incorrect tubing diameter or type Expected outcome: The tubing is correctly positioned within the detector sensing area. If proper tubing placement clears the alarm and the detector passes functional verification, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Sensor Area
steps.instructions: With the equipment out of clinical use, inspect accessible detector surfaces for: Moisture Blood or fluid residue Gel Dust Adhesive Cracks Damage that could interfere with sensing Clean only using approved methods. Expected outcome: The detector sensing surfaces are clean, dry, and physically intact. If approved cleaning restores normal detector function, troubleshooting can stop after testing.

steps.title: 5. Check Detector Cable and Connection
steps.instructions: Inspect the external detector cable and connectors for looseness, strain, contamination, or visible damage. Reseat approved connections if needed. Observe whether gentle movement of the cable causes recognition or alarm status to change. Expected outcome: The detector remains recognized and stable regardless of normal cable positioning. If correcting a loose external connection resolves the condition and testing passes, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 6. Verify Correct Detector Configuration
steps.instructions: Confirm the detector is connected to the expected system channel and the normal operating configuration matches the installed setup. Do not bypass the safety function or change protected thresholds. Expected outcome: The detector is correctly configured and enabled for the intended circuit. If an authorized configuration correction restores normal operation, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 7. Compare With Known-Good Components
steps.instructions: When permitted, compare operation using known-good compatible tubing, detector hardware, or external cable one component at a time. Expected outcome: The failure follows a replaceable external component or remains with the detector/system channel. If a faulty external component is identified and replaced, troubleshooting can stop after successful detector testing.

steps.title: 8. Perform Approved Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Use the appropriate approved detector test method and verify: Detector recognition Alarm activation when expected Alarm clearing when the test condition is removed Stable operation with tubing correctly seated Associated system response as applicable Do not invent or substitute unapproved bubble test methods. Expected outcome: The bubble detector and associated alarm pathway operate correctly during approved testing. If all checks pass, troubleshooting is complete.

steps.title: 9. Escalate an Unresolved Detector Failure
steps.instructions: If the detector fails testing, alarms intermittently without an identifiable external cause, or cannot be trusted, remove it from service. Do not disable the detector or troubleshoot internal sensing electronics at board level. Expected outcome: An unreliable air-detection safety function is not returned to clinical use.

CCR.Complaint: Perfusion reported repeated S5 bubble detector alarms during pre-case setup with no bubble visible in the test circuit.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the tubing was only partially seated in the detector sensing channel.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering correctly seated the tubing and verified normal detector recognition and successful approved alarm testing.

helpfulDetails: Whether alarm changes with cable movement
Whether the problem followed the circuit or detector

title: LivaNova S5 Heart-Lung Machine - Level Sensor Alarm or Sensor Will Not Calibrate
description: Troubleshoots level sensor alarms or calibration problems by checking sensor placement, reservoir interface, cleanliness, cabling, and configuration.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Reservoir Level
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot an unreliable level sensor while a patient depends on it as the active reservoir-level safeguard. Maintain direct clinical monitoring and follow the perfusion contingency plan using verified backup protection. Never disable a level alarm simply to continue a case. Expected outcome: Reservoir level remains safely managed independently of the suspect sensor. Once the sensor is isolated from active patient support, troubleshooting may continue.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether: The level alarm is active unexpectedly. The sensor is not recognized. Calibration will not complete. The alarm appears intermittently. The condition changes when the sensor is moved. The problem began after changing reservoirs or sensor position. Record the displayed message if present. Expected outcome: The failure is identified as placement, recognition, calibration, or intermittent sensing. If the sensor subsequently calibrates normally and passes verification, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 3. Verify Sensor Placement
steps.instructions: Inspect the position of the level sensor on the compatible reservoir. Confirm it is: At the intended sensing location Fully seated Properly oriented Flat against the required surface Not positioned over labels, seams, or obstructions that interfere with sensing Expected outcome: The level sensor is positioned correctly for the installed reservoir. If repositioning restores normal calibration and alarm function, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Reservoir Interface
steps.instructions: Check the sensing location for: Condensation Moisture Adhesive residue Surface contamination Damage Unexpected wall thickness or incompatible reservoir design Use only approved compatible components. Expected outcome: The reservoir surface at the sensing point is clean, dry, intact, and compatible. If correcting an interface problem restores sensing, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Sensor and Cable
steps.instructions: Examine the external sensor and cable for: Cracks Loose housing Damaged strain relief Cuts Fluid intrusion Connector damage Reseat the external connector if appropriate. Expected outcome: The sensor and external cabling are secure and physically intact. If reseating or replacing a damaged approved external component resolves the issue, troubleshooting can stop after testing.

steps.title: 6. Verify Normal Configuration
steps.instructions: Confirm the intended level sensor is selected and enabled in the normal system configuration. Verify that the correct sensor/channel is being used for the connected reservoir. Do not alter protected calibration parameters or alarm thresholds outside authorized procedures. Expected outcome: The configured sensor matches the physical setup. If an authorized configuration correction allows successful calibration, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 7. Compare With a Known-Good Setup
steps.instructions: When permitted, use a known-good compatible reservoir setup, sensor, or cable to isolate whether the failure follows the disposable interface or the sensor hardware. Expected outcome: The cause is isolated to an external component, setup, or the sensor/system channel. If an external component is identified as defective and replacement restores normal operation, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 8. Perform Approved Calibration and Alarm Verification
steps.instructions: Follow the approved normal calibration process and then verify the alarm responds appropriately to the approved test condition. Do not invent calibration methods or simulate reservoir conditions in an unapproved manner. Expected outcome: Calibration completes normally and the level alarm pathway operates predictably. If all checks pass, troubleshooting is complete.

steps.title: 9. Escalate Persistent Sensor Failure
steps.instructions: If the sensor will not calibrate, alarms intermittently, or cannot reliably detect the approved test condition, remove the affected function from service. Do not bypass the sensor or perform internal electronic adjustment without manufacturer-authorized procedures. Expected outcome: An unreliable level-sensing safety feature is not returned to patient care.

CCR.Complaint: Perfusion reported that the S5 level sensor would not complete calibration during setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the sensor mounted over a label on the reservoir rather than directly against the intended sensing surface.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering repositioned the sensor on the correct reservoir surface and verified successful calibration and alarm operation.

title: LivaNova S5 Heart-Lung Machine - Temperature Channel Missing, Inaccurate, or Unstable
description: Troubleshoots absent, inaccurate, or unstable temperature readings by checking probes, adapters, connections, channel selection, positioning, and known-good comparisons.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Use Verified Temperature Monitoring
steps.instructions: Do not rely on a temperature channel known to be missing, unstable, or inaccurate during patient support. Provide an alternate verified temperature-monitoring method before technical troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Patient temperature is monitored using reliable equipment while the affected channel is evaluated. Once the suspect channel is no longer required clinically, troubleshooting may continue.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Temperature Problem
steps.instructions: Determine whether the channel: Is completely absent. Displays an implausible value. Drifts slowly. Changes abruptly. Is intermittent when the cable moves. Differs from another clinically appropriate comparison source. Fails only on one probe or one system channel. Expected outcome: The problem is isolated to a missing signal, unstable signal, or suspected accuracy discrepancy. If readings are stable and consistent after reproducing the setup correctly, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Temperature Probe
steps.instructions: Inspect the probe and its accessible cable for: Cuts Kinks Damaged insulation Bent connector components Fluid intrusion Loose strain relief Visible contamination Confirm the probe is compatible with the intended system input. Expected outcome: The temperature probe and cable are compatible and physically intact. If replacing a damaged probe with a known-good compatible probe restores stable readings, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Check Probe and Adapter Connections
steps.instructions: Verify the probe is fully connected to the correct temperature input. Inspect any external adapter or extension cable used in the signal path. Reseat accessible connections and avoid unnecessary adapters when testing. Expected outcome: The complete external temperature signal path is securely connected. If reseating a connector restores stable readings, troubleshooting can stop after testing.

steps.title: 5. Verify Probe Position and Test Conditions
steps.instructions: Ensure any comparison test uses the probe in a stable, appropriate test environment. Do not compare probes exposed to different thermal conditions and assume the channel is inaccurate. Expected outcome: The reference and suspect readings are compared under equivalent, controlled conditions. If the apparent discrepancy disappears under comparable conditions, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 6. Compare With Known-Good Components
steps.instructions: Use a known-good compatible probe on the suspect S5 channel. When appropriate, test the suspect probe on another verified compatible channel. Expected outcome: The problem follows the probe/accessory or remains with the S5 channel. If the problem follows the probe, replace the defective external component and verify normal operation.

steps.title: 7. Verify Channel Selection and Configuration
steps.instructions: Confirm the displayed temperature source corresponds to the physical input being tested and that the expected channel is enabled in the normal configuration. Do not change protected calibration constants without authorization. Expected outcome: The displayed channel matches the connected probe and normal system configuration. If correcting an authorized channel selection resolves the problem, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 8. Perform Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Using approved test equipment or an approved comparison method, verify: The channel is present. The displayed value is stable. Cable movement does not cause dropouts. A known-good probe produces consistent results. Other channels remain unaffected. Do not claim calibration compliance unless the required calibrated test equipment and manufacturer procedure have been used. Expected outcome: The temperature channel provides a stable and credible signal under controlled testing. If all checks pass, troubleshooting is complete.

steps.title: 9. Escalate an Unresolved Temperature Channel Fault
steps.instructions: If the channel remains missing, unstable, or cannot be verified against approved test equipment after external components are ruled out, remove the affected function from service. Do not perform internal component replacement or calibration adjustment outside authorized procedures. Expected outcome: An unverified temperature channel is not returned to clinical monitoring.

CCR.Complaint: Perfusion reported that one S5 temperature channel intermittently disappeared during equipment setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a damaged temperature-probe cable that opened intermittently when flexed near the connector.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering replaced the probe with a known-good compatible probe and verified stable temperature indication during controlled testing.

title: LivaNova S5 Heart-Lung Machine - Pressure Channel Will Not Zero or Displays Incorrectly
description: Troubleshoots pressure channels that will not zero or display correctly by checking transducers, cables, stopcocks, setup, connections, and configuration.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Use Verified Pressure Monitoring
steps.instructions: Do not rely on an S5 pressure channel that cannot be zeroed or produces questionable values during patient care. Establish an alternate verified pressure-monitoring method before technical troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Clinically important pressure remains monitored independently of the suspect channel. Once the affected channel is removed from patient dependency, troubleshooting may continue.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Pressure Problem
steps.instructions: Determine whether the channel: Will not zero. Displays an offset at atmospheric pressure. Shows unstable or drifting values. Is absent. Responds incorrectly to pressure changes. Fails only with one transducer or cable. Record the displayed condition or message. Expected outcome: The failure is categorized as zeroing, signal, stability, or accessory related. If the channel zeros normally and passes controlled verification, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Transducer Setup
steps.instructions: Inspect the pressure transducer and fluid path used for testing. Confirm: The correct compatible transducer is being used. The transducer is properly connected. The reference port is opened appropriately for the normal zeroing process. Stopcocks and tubing are arranged correctly. There is no obvious fluid blockage or trapped pressure during zeroing. Expected outcome: The transducer is actually exposed to the correct zero-reference condition. If correcting the external fluid setup allows successful zeroing, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Transducer and Cable
steps.instructions: Check the transducer, interface cable, and connectors for: Damage Bent contacts Fluid contamination Loose connections Cable cuts Strain Corrosion Replace visibly compromised external components with approved compatible parts. Expected outcome: The external pressure-sensing components are intact and securely connected. If replacement of a damaged transducer or cable restores normal operation, troubleshooting can stop after testing.

steps.title: 5. Reseat the Pressure Connection
steps.instructions: With the equipment out of clinical use, disconnect and reconnect the approved external pressure interface. Ensure the connector is fully seated. Expected outcome: The pressure channel detects the connected transducer consistently. If reseating restores stable operation and successful zeroing, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 6. Compare With Known-Good Components
steps.instructions: Test a known-good compatible pressure transducer and cable on the suspect channel. When appropriate, test the suspect external components on another verified compatible channel. Expected outcome: The fault follows an external transducer/cable or remains with the S5 pressure channel. If the external component is identified as defective, replace it and verify the channel.

steps.title: 7. Verify Channel Selection and Configuration
steps.instructions: Confirm the physical pressure input matches the displayed channel and that the channel is enabled in the normal system configuration. Do not alter protected calibration parameters or pressure scaling without authorized procedures. Expected outcome: The configured channel corresponds to the connected pressure input. If correcting an authorized configuration mismatch resolves the issue, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 8. Perform Controlled Pressure Verification
steps.instructions: Using approved pressure test equipment and the appropriate manufacturer procedure, verify: Successful zeroing Stable baseline Predictable response to applied test pressure Return to zero No dropout during cable movement Do not state that the channel is calibrated unless calibration has actually been completed using the required procedure and calibrated equipment. Expected outcome: The pressure channel zeros correctly and provides stable, credible readings during controlled testing. If all checks pass, troubleshooting is complete.

steps.title: 9. Escalate an Unresolved Pressure Fault
steps.instructions: If the channel cannot zero or readings remain inaccurate after external transducer, tubing, cable, and setup causes are eliminated, remove the affected monitoring function from service. Do not perform internal electronic adjustment without authorized procedures. Expected outcome: An unverified pressure channel is not returned to patient monitoring.

CCR.Complaint: Perfusion reported that one S5 pressure channel would not zero during pre-case setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external stopcock arrangement left residual pressure on the transducer during the zero attempt.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering corrected the test setup and verified successful zeroing and stable pressure response using approved test equipment.

title: LivaNova S5 Heart-Lung Machine - Gas Blender, Timer, or Cardioplegia Module Communication Failure
description: Troubleshoots loss of communication with gas blender, timer, or cardioplegia functions by checking module power, cabling, connections, and system configuration.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Provide Alternate Clinical Capability
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot a failed gas-management, timer, or cardioplegia communication function while the patient depends on it. Immediately follow the perfusion contingency plan and provide a verified alternate method for the affected function. If gas delivery or cardioplegia control itself is unreliable, treat the condition as a clinical equipment failure rather than only a display or communication problem. Expected outcome: The affected clinical function is maintained using reliable alternate equipment or workflow. Once the module is no longer required for active patient support, troubleshooting may continue.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Function Has Failed
steps.instructions: Identify whether the communication problem affects: Gas blender Timer Cardioplegia module Multiple modules simultaneously Determine whether the module: Does not appear at startup. Appears and then disappears. Operates locally but is not shown by the S5. Loses communication when equipment is moved. Fails after a configuration change. Record any displayed message exactly. Expected outcome: The fault is localized to one module or a shared communication path. If normal communication is restored and remains stable through repeated testing, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 3. Verify Module Power and Readiness
steps.instructions: Confirm the affected module is powered and completes its normal startup behavior. Inspect obvious power indicators and normal controls. Expected outcome: The module itself is powered and available to communicate. If restoring external module power resolves communication, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect External Communication Connections
steps.instructions: With the system out of clinical use, inspect accessible module communication cables and connectors for: Loose seating Damaged connector housings Bent or contaminated contacts visible externally Cable strain Cuts or crushing Fluid intrusion Reseat approved external connectors. Expected outcome: Communication cabling is securely connected and free of visible damage. If reseating a connection restores reliable communication, troubleshooting can stop after repeated testing.

steps.title: 5. Determine Whether the Failure Is Shared
steps.instructions: If multiple modules are affected, inspect common external communication paths, shared connection points, and system-wide power conditions before assuming several modules failed independently. Expected outcome: The failure is identified as module-specific or associated with a shared external path. If correcting a shared external connection restores all modules, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 6. Compare With Known-Good Components
steps.instructions: When approved and compatible, substitute a known-good communication cable or module connection one component at a time. Do not alter device identity or protected network settings without authorization. Expected outcome: The communication loss follows an external cable/module or remains with the original system connection. If a defective external cable is identified and replaced, troubleshooting can stop after final testing.

steps.title: 7. Verify Normal System Configuration
steps.instructions: Confirm the installed module is expected in the active S5 configuration and has not been intentionally disabled or removed. Do not enter restricted service configuration or change protected communication parameters without appropriate authorization. Expected outcome: The installed hardware and normal configuration agree. If correcting an authorized configuration issue restores module communication, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 8. Perform Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After communication is restored, verify: The module appears consistently. Status information updates normally. Commands or data expected through the normal interface are exchanged appropriately. Communication remains stable during repeated startup. No related module alarms remain. For gas or cardioplegia functions, complete applicable functional checks before clinical use. Expected outcome: Communication and the associated clinical function are stable and repeatable. If all checks pass, troubleshooting is complete.

steps.title: 9. Escalate Persistent Communication Failure
steps.instructions: If a module remains unavailable after external power, cabling, connections, and configuration are ruled out, remove the affected equipment from service. Do not troubleshoot internal communication boards or module electronics at board level. Expected outcome: A system with unresolved loss of a required clinical function is not returned to use.

CCR.Complaint: Perfusion reported that the S5 cardioplegia module was not appearing on the system during pre-case setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the module communication cable partially disconnected after the system had been relocated.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering reseated and secured the cable and verified stable module communication and normal cardioplegia-system functional checks.

helpfulDetails: Whether one or multiple modules lost communication

title: LivaNova S5 Heart-Lung Machine - Battery Backup, Power Supply, or CAN-Bus Communication Problem
description: Troubleshoots backup-power, external power, and system communication problems using power-source checks, module isolation, connections, and safe functional verification.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain a Fully Functional Backup System
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot unstable S5 power or system communication while a patient depends on the affected equipment. A loss of power distribution or shared communication can affect multiple perfusion functions simultaneously. Follow the perfusion contingency plan and transition to verified backup support as required. If there is smoke, odor, overheating, arcing, liquid intrusion, or repeated power loss, remove power when clinically safe and take the system out of service. Expected outcome: Patient support is maintained independently of the suspect S5 power or communication system. Once safely isolated from clinical use, troubleshooting may continue.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Failure Pattern
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem involves: Failure on AC power Failure on battery-supported power Battery not charging Unexpected transition to backup power Multiple modules disappearing simultaneously Intermittent module communication Complete system restart A single module versus system-wide CAN-bus communication loss Record all displayed messages and indicator states. Expected outcome: The failure is categorized as source-power, backup-power, or shared communication related. If the system remains stable through repeated controlled tests after a correctable external condition is found, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 3. Verify Facility AC Power
steps.instructions: Inspect the power cord, plug, strain relief, and accessible input connections. Confirm the receptacle is powered using approved test equipment or a known-good source. Check whether the problem occurs at one outlet only or follows the S5. Expected outcome: A stable facility AC source is confirmed. If an outlet or external power problem is identified and correction restores normal operation, troubleshooting can stop after system verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect External Power Connections
steps.instructions: With the S5 removed from service, inspect all accessible power connections associated with the console and connected modules. Look for: Loose connectors Damage Heat discoloration Contamination Damaged cord insulation Strain at connection points Do not open internal power supplies. Expected outcome: External power connections are fully seated and free of visible damage. If correcting an external power connection restores reliable operation, troubleshooting can stop after testing.

steps.title: 5. Evaluate Battery-Supported Operation
steps.instructions: Using approved procedures, determine whether the system: Recognizes backup power. Indicates charging appropriately. Transfers between AC and backup power normally. Remains stable during the approved backup-power test. Do not intentionally run backup batteries to exhaustion. Expected outcome: Backup power is recognized and supports the system as intended during the approved test. If a replaceable approved battery component is confirmed defective and replacement restores normal operation, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 6. Inspect External Communication Connections
steps.instructions: Because shared CAN-bus communication problems may affect multiple modules, inspect accessible intermodule communication cables and connectors for: Partial seating Damage Fluid contamination Cable strain Crushed sections Loose retaining hardware Reseat only approved external communication connections. Expected outcome: External communication connections are secure and undamaged. If reseating a communication connection restores all affected modules and stability is confirmed, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 7. Determine Whether One Module Is Disrupting the System
steps.instructions: If permitted by approved service procedures, identify whether the communication problem occurs only when a specific external module or cable is connected. Use controlled isolation or known-good substitution without altering protected internal bus termination or configuration. Do not remove modules required for active clinical support. Expected outcome: The problem is isolated to a specific external module/cable or remains system-wide. If a defective external module connection or cable is identified and correction restores stable communication, troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 8. Verify Normal Configuration and Module Population
steps.instructions: Confirm that connected modules match the normal system configuration and that no component has been intentionally removed, disabled, or reconfigured. Do not change restricted CAN-bus parameters, internal addressing, or termination. Expected outcome: Installed modules and the authorized configuration are consistent. If an authorized configuration correction resolves communication, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final System Verification
steps.instructions: After correction, verify: Stable operation on AC power. Appropriate battery/backup status. Normal transfer behavior using approved procedures. All required modules are recognized. Communication remains stable through repeated startup. No unexplained system resets occur. Required pumps, sensors, displays, and alarms function appropriately. Complete all applicable return-to-service testing. Expected outcome: The complete S5 system remains stable across approved power and communication checks. If all checks pass, troubleshooting is complete.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Power or CAN-Bus Problems
steps.instructions: If the system has repeated power loss, unexplained resets, battery-transfer problems, or persistent communication loss after external causes are ruled out, stop troubleshooting. Do not open internal power supplies, repair bus electronics, change internal termination, or replace circuit boards without authorized service procedures. Expected outcome: A system with unresolved shared power or communication risk remains unavailable for patient use.

CCR.Complaint: Perfusion reported that several S5 modules intermittently disappeared from the console during pre-case setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a shared external communication connector partially seated after the system had been moved.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering reseated and secured the connector and verified stable module communication, repeated startup, and normal system operation.

helpfulDetails: AC or battery condition when failure occurred

title: LivaNova S5 Heart-Lung Machine - Cardioplegia Delivery Ratio or Volume Is Inaccurate Although the Module Is Online
description: Troubleshoots inaccurate cardioplegia ratio or delivered volume caused by setup, tubing, occlusion, pump, sensor, configuration, or accessory-related conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Cardioplegia Capability
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot an unreliable cardioplegia delivery function while a patient depends on it. Ensure the perfusion team has an alternate verified method for cardioplegia delivery before Clinical Engineering begins troubleshooting. If the inaccurate ratio or volume was observed during a case, preserve the reported settings and observations when possible without delaying patient care. Expected outcome: Patient care is transferred to a safe, verified cardioplegia delivery method and the affected system is available for controlled evaluation.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Reported Condition
steps.instructions: Obtain the reported programmed ratio, intended volume, displayed delivered volume, and any independent measurement used to determine that delivery was inaccurate. Determine whether the problem affects: Ratio calculation Total delivered volume One solution channel only Both cardioplegia components Displayed information versus actual measured delivery A specific disposable setup or repeated setups Do not assume the module itself is defective solely because the displayed and expected values differ. Expected outcome: The discrepancy is clearly defined and reproducible enough to guide testing.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Cardioplegia Circuit and Disposable Setup
steps.instructions: With the system out of clinical use, inspect the external cardioplegia tubing and associated disposables for: Incorrect tubing installation Reversed or crossed tubing paths Kinks or compression Loose connections Air in the fluid path Improperly seated tubing in the pump mechanism Damaged or stretched tubing Clamps or stopcocks restricting flow Incorrect disposable selection for the intended setup Correct any obvious external setup problem and repeat the controlled test. Expected outcome: Tubing and disposables are correctly installed, unrestricted, and appropriate for the configured delivery system. If delivery becomes accurate, troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 4. Verify Pump Direction and Channel Assignment
steps.instructions: Confirm that each pump involved in cardioplegia delivery is operating in the intended direction and corresponds to the correct solution path. Verify that the physical tubing paths match the displayed or configured pump assignments. A correct electronic ratio cannot produce the intended mixture if the tubing is connected to the wrong pump or solution source. Expected outcome: Each pump moves the intended solution in the correct direction and channel assignments match the physical circuit.

steps.title: 5. Check External Pump Loading and Mechanical Engagement
steps.instructions: Inspect the pump head and externally accessible loading area for: Tubing not fully seated Inconsistent tubing compression Foreign material Visible wear or damage Pump-head obstruction Improperly secured pump components Do not disassemble the pump mechanism beyond normal approved access. Expected outcome: The pump mechanism operates smoothly with the tubing correctly loaded and no visible external cause of inaccurate delivery.

steps.title: 6. Verify Cardioplegia Controls and Configuration
steps.instructions: Review the cardioplegia-related settings available through normal authorized operation. Confirm that the intended ratio, delivery mode, pump selections, and applicable configuration match the clinical setup being tested. Check for unintended changes made between cases or after servicing. Do not enter restricted service menus or alter protected calibration values without approved service documentation. Expected outcome: The displayed settings and normal configuration agree with the intended cardioplegia delivery setup.

steps.title: 7. Perform a Controlled Volume Comparison
steps.instructions: Using an approved bench setup and appropriate measurement equipment, run a controlled delivery test without a patient connected. Compare the commanded delivery with the independently measured output. If separate pumps contribute to the mixture, evaluate their outputs individually when this can be done using approved procedures. Use fresh, correctly installed tubing if the disposable circuit is suspect. Expected outcome: Independently measured delivery agrees with the commanded ratio and volume. If it does, the system may proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 8. Substitute Known-Good External Components
steps.instructions: If the discrepancy remains, substitute known-good compatible external components where practical, such as: Tubing set Fluid container or source External accessory associated with the cardioplegia setup Another verified pump position or compatible module arrangement, if permitted by approved procedures Change one variable at a time so the cause remains identifiable. Expected outcome: A faulty disposable or external component is identified, or the problem remains associated with the equipment.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After correcting the cause, repeat a controlled cardioplegia delivery test across the functions involved in the complaint. Verify: Pump operation Correct flow direction Ratio selection Delivered volume indication Independent measured output Relevant alarms and indicators No leaks, restrictions, or abnormal mechanical behavior Document the test equipment and results according to facility practice. Expected outcome: Cardioplegia delivery operates consistently and agrees with the intended setup. If verification passes, troubleshooting is complete.

steps.title: 10. Stop and Escalate if Accuracy Cannot Be Verified
steps.instructions: If delivery remains inaccurate, inconsistent, or cannot be independently verified, do not return the cardioplegia function to clinical service. Expected outcome: The affected equipment is removed from service rather than being used with uncertain cardioplegia delivery accuracy.

CCR.Complaint: Perfusion reported that the S5 cardioplegia module remained online but the delivered mixture volume did not agree with the programmed ratio and expected output.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the cardioplegia tubing incorrectly seated in one pump channel, producing inconsistent delivery during controlled testing.
CCR.Resolution: The tubing was reinstalled correctly and controlled delivery testing confirmed consistent ratio and volume performance before the system was returned to service.

helpfulDetails: Any restrictions, clamps, or kinks found

title: LivaNova S5 Heart-Lung Machine - Case Record or Data-Management Export Fails
description: Troubleshoots failed case-data export caused by media, connections, destination availability, configuration, storage, or external data-management system problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Separate Data Failure From Pumping Function
steps.instructions: Do not interrupt active extracorporeal support solely to troubleshoot case-data export. If the S5 is currently supporting a patient and pumping functions remain normal, document the export problem and defer technical troubleshooting until the system can be safely evaluated without affecting patient care. Expected outcome: Clinical support continues safely and data troubleshooting occurs only when it cannot interfere with perfusion operation.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Export Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether: A case record is visible locally but will not export No case record is being created Export begins but stops The destination does not recognize the file Only one case is affected All exports fail The problem occurs with removable media, network transfer, or another data-management path Record any exact on-screen message without interpreting it beyond what is displayed. Expected outcome: The failure is narrowed to record creation, local storage, transfer, or destination access.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Case Record Exists Locally
steps.instructions: Using normal authorized controls, confirm that the expected case or record is present and can be opened or reviewed locally where applicable. If the record itself is missing, an export problem cannot be distinguished from a case-recording or storage problem until that issue is investigated. Expected outcome: The intended case record exists locally and is available for export.

steps.title: 4. Inspect External Connections and Export Media
steps.instructions: For a physical export path, inspect the applicable external components for: Loose connection Damaged connector Bent or contaminated contacts Damaged cable Improperly inserted media Unsupported or suspect media Visible physical damage Reconnect securely and retry using normal controls. Expected outcome: The physical export connection or media is correctly installed and undamaged.

steps.title: 5. Try a Known-Good Approved Export Device or Cable
steps.instructions: When applicable, test with a known-good compatible cable, removable storage device, interface, or destination connection that is approved for the environment. Do not connect unapproved personal storage devices or alter cybersecurity controls. Expected outcome: Export succeeds with the known-good component, identifying the original external accessory or connection as the cause.

steps.title: 6. Verify Available Storage and Record Status
steps.instructions: Check normal user-accessible indications for local storage availability and whether the case record has completed saving. Avoid deleting clinical records merely to create space unless this is performed under the facility's approved data-retention and service procedures. Expected outcome: The source record is complete and the device has adequate normal operating storage for the required data function.

steps.title: 7. Check Normal Data-Management Configuration
steps.instructions: Review authorized, normally accessible settings relevant to the export path. Verify that the selected export destination, data-management connection, and applicable communication settings match the intended workflow. Do not modify restricted network parameters, cybersecurity settings, service configuration, or protected system files without authorization. Expected outcome: The export destination and normal configuration correspond to the intended data path.

steps.title: 8. Verify the Receiving System or Destination
steps.instructions: If data is being sent to another workstation, server, or clinical data-management system, determine whether that destination is available. Check: Destination powered on Network or interface connection present Other systems able to reach the destination Adequate destination storage if this can be verified No known infrastructure outage Correct destination selected Coordinate with IT or the responsible clinical data-management team when appropriate. Expected outcome: The receiving system is available and capable of accepting data.

steps.title: 9. Perform a Controlled Test Export
steps.instructions: Using a suitable non-patient test record or approved test workflow, perform another export. Determine whether the failure: Follows one specific record Occurs with all records Occurs only through one export method Occurs only with one destination Avoid unnecessary copying of protected patient information during testing. Expected outcome: The export completes and the resulting record is accessible at the intended destination. If so, troubleshooting can stop after documentation.

steps.title: 10. Stop and Escalate Persistent Data Failures
steps.instructions: If records are present locally but repeatedly fail to export after external connections, media, destination availability, and normal configuration have been verified, escalate the issue. Do not modify internal storage, operating-system files, protected networking, or data-management software outside approved service procedures. Expected outcome: Persistent data problems are escalated without risking stored clinical information or system operation.

CCR.Complaint: Perfusion reported that completed S5 case records were available on the system but would not export to the designated data-management destination.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external data cable partially disconnected at the receiving interface.
CCR.Resolution: The connection was reseated and secured, and a controlled test record exported successfully and was verified at the destination.

helpfulDetails: Whether one or all records are affected

title: LivaNova S5 Heart-Lung Machine - Emergency Hand Crank or Pump Coupling Will Not Engage
description: Troubleshoots failure of an emergency hand crank or external pump coupling to engage because of alignment, obstruction, damage, or incorrect positioning.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Blood Flow
steps.instructions: A hand-crank engagement problem can compromise the ability to maintain circulation during a pump-drive failure. Do not troubleshoot the affected pump while it is supporting a patient. Ensure the perfusion team has an alternate verified means of maintaining required flow before Clinical Engineering evaluates the problem. If the failure occurred during a case, remove the affected pump position from clinical dependence before testing. Expected outcome: Patient circulation is supported by a verified alternate method and the affected pump can be safely evaluated.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Engagement Problem
steps.instructions: Ask the perfusionist whether: The crank would not insert It inserted but would not lock or couple It coupled but slipped The pump would not rotate Excessive force was required The problem affected one pump position or multiple positions Inspect the crank and coupling without forcing them together. Expected outcome: The failure is identified as an insertion, alignment, coupling, retention, or rotation problem.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Correct Emergency Crank and Intended Pump Position
steps.instructions: Confirm that the available hand crank or manual-drive accessory is the correct approved accessory for the S5 configuration and intended pump position. Check for mislabeled, misplaced, or incompatible accessories stored with the system. Expected outcome: The correct emergency accessory is being used with the intended pump mechanism.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Hand Crank
steps.instructions: Examine the emergency crank for: Bent shaft Damaged engagement features Cracks Excessive wear Corrosion Debris Missing or loose external parts Evidence that it was dropped or forced Do not attempt to straighten, machine, or modify the crank. Expected outcome: The crank is physically intact and capable of engaging normally.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Pump Coupling
steps.instructions: With the equipment safely out of service and the pump stationary, inspect the accessible coupling point for: Debris or foreign material Damage Misalignment Deformed engagement surfaces Obstructions Loose externally accessible parts Do not insert tools into the coupling or disassemble the drive mechanism. Expected outcome: The coupling is unobstructed and appears mechanically intact.

steps.title: 6. Verify Pump Position and Mechanical Alignment
steps.instructions: Ensure the pump mechanism is in the proper stationary condition for emergency crank engagement according to normal approved operation. Gently align the crank with the coupling without forcing it. Small rotational adjustment may allow engagement if the mating features were initially misaligned. Never use excessive force. Expected outcome: The crank seats and couples positively using normal hand pressure. If it engages correctly and remains secure, proceed to functional verification.

steps.title: 7. Check for Binding Before Applying Manual Rotation
steps.instructions: Once engagement is confirmed, carefully assess whether the pump can be rotated manually using an approved unloaded or controlled test setup. Stop if there is: Abnormal resistance Grinding Binding Intermittent locking Slipping Visible coupling movement without pump rotation Expected outcome: Manual rotation is smooth, mechanically consistent, and directly drives the intended pump mechanism.

steps.title: 8. Compare With Another Verified Pump Position or Known-Good Crank
steps.instructions: If available and permitted, compare the affected pump position with another equivalent verified pump position. A known-good compatible crank may help determine whether the problem follows the crank or remains with the pump coupling. Do not interchange accessories if compatibility is uncertain. Expected outcome: The fault is isolated to either the emergency crank/accessory or the affected pump position.

steps.title: 9. Verify Normal Powered Pump Operation
steps.instructions: After completing the mechanical inspection and with the emergency crank removed, verify normal powered pump operation in a controlled setup. Confirm: Smooth rotation Normal start and stop No abnormal noise No visible mechanical instability Normal applicable status indications A pump that binds during manual operation should not be considered acceptable merely because powered operation appears normal. Expected outcome: Both manual emergency drive and normal powered operation function reliably.

steps.title: 10. Stop and Escalate if Engagement Is Unreliable
steps.instructions: If the hand crank cannot be positively engaged, slips, binds, or requires excessive force, remove the affected equipment from service. Emergency manual-drive capability must not be assumed to be available if it cannot be demonstrated during testing. Expected outcome: Equipment with unreliable emergency pumping capability is prevented from returning to clinical use.

CCR.Complaint: Perfusion reported that the emergency hand crank could not be fully engaged with one S5 pump position during a pre-use check.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found debris in the externally accessible pump coupling that prevented the crank from seating completely.
CCR.Resolution: The obstruction was removed without disassembly, and the crank was verified to engage securely and rotate the pump smoothly before powered operation was also functionally tested.

helpfulDetails: Whether the crank inserted, locked, slipped, or bound

title: LivaNova S5 Heart-Lung Machine - Remote Display and Pump Status Indicators Do Not Agree
description: Troubleshoots disagreement between remote display information and pump status caused by connections, communication, configuration, display update, or component synchronization problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Use the Verified Local Pump Status
steps.instructions: Conflicting pump indications can create a serious perfusion safety hazard. Do not rely on a remote display whose information does not agree with directly verified pump operation. If the system is in clinical use, the perfusionist should use the verified primary/local pump information and established alternate monitoring until the discrepancy is resolved. Do not disconnect active system components during patient support unless specifically directed by an approved clinical contingency procedure. Expected outcome: Patient care is based only on verified pump information and the questionable remote indication is not used for clinical decisions.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Indications Disagree
steps.instructions: Identify the exact discrepancy, such as: Pump running versus stopped Displayed pump speed Pump identity or position Direction of rotation Alarm or status indication Remote display frozen on an earlier value One pump incorrect while others agree All pump information incorrect Compare the remote indication with direct observation and the primary control or local display. Expected outcome: The affected status parameter and pump position are clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Determine Whether the Remote Display Is Updating
steps.instructions: Observe whether unrelated information on the remote display changes normally. Check whether: The clock or other dynamic information changes Other pump values update Controls or pages respond normally The displayed value appears frozen Updates occur only intermittently This helps distinguish a single-channel status problem from loss of the complete communication path. Expected outcome: The problem is classified as a frozen display, intermittent communication issue, or disagreement limited to a particular pump/status value.

steps.title: 4. Inspect External Communication Connections
steps.instructions: Once the system is safely available for technical evaluation, inspect external cables and connectors between the relevant system components. Look for: Loose plugs Partially seated connectors Damaged cable jackets Bent or contaminated contacts Strain on connectors Incorrect connection points Evidence that equipment was recently moved or reconfigured Reseat only connectors that are intended for normal external service access. Expected outcome: External communication connections are secure and physically intact. If indications synchronize afterward, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 5. Check Power and Status of the Remote Display
steps.instructions: Verify that the remote display and associated external components have stable power and complete normal startup. Look for: Intermittent power Rebooting Flickering Incomplete startup Unexpected blanking Abnormal external indicator behavior If the display itself is unstable, address the power or display problem before interpreting pump-status discrepancies. Expected outcome: The remote display remains powered and stable throughout testing.

steps.title: 6. Verify Pump and Display Assignments
steps.instructions: Through normal authorized controls, confirm that pump identities and displayed assignments correspond to the actual physical pump positions. A configuration or assignment mismatch may cause valid information from one pump to appear to represent another. Do not alter restricted system configuration without approved documentation and authorization. Expected outcome: Each displayed pump identity matches the intended physical pump and control channel.

steps.title: 7. Compare Multiple Pump Positions
steps.instructions: Using a controlled test setup, compare local and remote indications for each available pump position. Start and stop pumps individually as permitted and observe whether the corresponding remote indication changes correctly. This helps determine whether the problem follows: One pump One connection One display field The entire remote interface Expected outcome: Each tested pump produces the corresponding status change on both the local and remote displays.

steps.title: 8. Substitute Known-Good External Components Where Permitted
steps.instructions: If the problem is isolated to an external communication cable or interchangeable accessory, substitute a known-good compatible component. Do not interchange internal modules or open system enclosures as part of this external troubleshooting process. Expected outcome: If synchronization is restored, the substituted external component identifies the likely cause.

steps.title: 9. Verify Alarm and Status Communication
steps.instructions: In a controlled non-patient setup, verify relevant status transitions and applicable alarms through the complete intended display path. Confirm that the remote display: Updates when pump state changes Identifies the correct pump Does not retain stale status Returns to the expected state after testing Expected outcome: Local and remote indications remain synchronized during all tested status changes.

steps.title: 10. Stop and Escalate Any Persistent Disagreement
steps.instructions: If remote and local pump indications still disagree, do not return the affected remote display function to clinical reliance. A remote display that intermittently or consistently shows incorrect pump status must be treated as unreliable even if the pump itself operates correctly. Expected outcome: The unreliable display or associated equipment is removed from service or clearly isolated from clinical use pending repair.

CCR.Complaint: Perfusion reported that one S5 pump showed a running condition locally while the remote display continued to indicate that the pump was stopped.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external communication cable at the remote display connection partially seated, causing intermittent status updates.
CCR.Resolution: The cable was fully reseated and secured, and controlled start/stop testing confirmed matching pump status on the local and remote displays before return to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether the display was frozen or updating
